backends/base.py.description: The lowering + lifecycle contract. Phase 1: emit only. Phase 5 (parity): grown to a per-target lifecycle (emit + uninstall + doctor + recompose_from_lock + lock helpers) so Goose and Pi reach feature-completeness, not just Claude. Backends receive only the IR and/or project path; they return written paths or neutral result dataclasses. No manifest/anchor/profile/schema access. The neutral UninstallResult/DoctorReport dataclasses are declared here so all backends + the CLI share one shape.

cli.py.description: Additive, opt-in CLI. Phase 1: a single implicit 'compile'. Phase 3/4 add goose/pi to the backend registry. Phase 5 (parity): grows into a subcommand dispatcher reaching FULL parity with the plugin's composer.py — compile | uninstall | doctor | from-lock | profile {list|inspect|save|create|edit|delete} — plus --allow-injection/--force where they apply. Keeps `system2 compile` (no subcommand) back-compatible. The claude-code path of every verb reproduces the frozen oracle's args/exit-codes/stdout/stderr byte-for-byte (CLI-contract goldens) so the plugin shim can run on it. tools/build_bundle.py.description: Phase 5 (convergence): the deterministic bundler. Generates the vendored, stdlib-only bundle the plugin ships by copying the compiler's product subtree (ir/ + backends/ + plugin_adapter) verbatim into plugin/scripts/_system2_compiler/ and writing BUNDLE.json with the compiler-source hash. A pure copy (no import rewriting) so the vendored tree's module-boundary + stdlib-only properties are EXACTLY the compiler's and byte-identical Claude output is guaranteed by construction. Lives in the compiler repo (test/build tooling, not a product module). bundled_at is excluded from the hash so a re-bundle of identical source is hash-stable.

tools/check_bundle_fresh.py.description: Phase 5 (G8/NFR-006): the CI hash/staleness guard. Regenerates the bundle from the current compiler source into a temp dir, hashes it, and compares to the committed plugin/scripts/_system2_compiler/ + its BUNDLE.json. FAILS when they differ ('vendored bundle is stale: regenerate via tools/build_bundle.py'). Deterministic (the bundler is a pure copy; bundled_at excluded from the hash). The machine-enforced cross-repo freshness check — a stale bundle cannot merge.

Same boundary as claude_code: imports only ir.graph + backends.base + backends._yaml + stdlib; reads its own backends/capabilities/goose.json data file; never reads manifests/anchor-map/profiles/schema. backends/_yaml.py.description: Phase 3: internal, stdlib-only deterministic block-YAML serializer (emit-only; no parser). Supports the closed recipe subset: mappings, sequences, scalars (str/int/bool/None), and '|' literal block scalars for multi-line instructions/prompt. Fixed 2-space indent, conservative double-quote predicate, LF endings, single trailing newline, insertion-ordered keys (the emitter controls order for determinism). Falls back to a JSON-compatible quoting for any un-block-formattable value. Correctness is gated empirically by 'goose recipe validate' in the test suite, not by a hand-written full YAML spec. Backend-internal; consumed by backends/goose.py only.

backends/_degradation.py.description: Phase 4 (PG6): the shared, descriptor-driven degradation helper. Backend-agnostic; lifts the per-capability report record assembly + the status->flags rule out of claude_code._build_degradation_report and goose._build_degradation_report so all three backends (claude_code/goose/pi) share one source of truth. Internal, stdlib-only, no I/O, no ir/* import (a backend hands it ir.capabilities-as-data + its own parsed descriptor). BYTE-PRESERVING: it reproduces both existing reports exactly — each backend keeps its own envelope + 'fields' selection so the serialized bytes of the claude-code lock degradation_report and system2.goose.lock.json are UNCHANGED. The status->flags rule is total over the four-value enum (native=>enforced:true,gated:false; adapted=>enforced:false,gated:true; advisory/unsupported=>both false), making Pi's MIXED status correct by construction.

public_exports.signature: build_capability_records(descriptor: dict, ir_capability_union: set[str], *, fields: tuple[str, ...], allow_native: bool = True) -> dict[str, dict]  # ordered {cap: {<fields...>}} in descriptor order filtered to IR-present; status/mechanism from the descriptor; enforced:=status=='native'; gated:=status=='adapted'; raises (no silent drop) on an IR-present cap absent from the descriptor; raises when allow_native is False and a status is 'native' (goose)

backends/pi.py.description: Phase 4: the Pi backend (third backend; the first MIXED-status backend). Lowers the SAME System2Graph onto a generated Pi TypeScript extension + Pi context/skill/prompt markdown. Same boundary as claude_code/goose: imports only ir.graph + backends._degradation + backends.base + stdlib; reads its own backends/capabilities/pi.json data file; never reads manifests/anchor-map/profiles/schema; never consumes ir.base_template / ir.overlay_inputs (renders from structured IR fields only). The compiler emits TS/markdown/JSON as TEXT — no node/TS/third-party in the compiler (node/pi only in TESTS). ENFORCEMENT: enforce-lease/block-dangerous/protect-sensitive are NATIVE via the generated extension's on('tool_call') handler (returns {block:true,reason} before the tool runs; Pi has no built-in permission system, so the handler IS the gate); budget is ADAPTED (on('agent_end') reporting); format/typecheck are ADVISORY (SYSTEM.md instruction). Backend owns DEFAULT dangerous-command + sensitive-path pattern sets (mirroring goose._DANGEROUS_COMMANDS, keeping the IR neutral); enforce-lease uses role write_scope when present, else is wired-but-unscoped and reported honestly. Output is a pure function of the IR (no timestamps); deterministic, escaped TS/markdown text.

public_exports.signature: class PiBackend(Backend) { name = 'pi'; def emit(self, ir: System2Graph, project_path: str) -> list[str] }

backends/capabilities/pi.json.description: Phase 4: per-capability status descriptor for the pi backend. Same schema as claude_code.json/goose.json. The first MIXED descriptor: enforce-lease/block-dangerous/protect-sensitive = native (generated extension on('tool_call') hard-block before the tool runs; Pi has no built-in permission system); budget = adapted (on('agent_end') reporting, not a block); format/typecheck = advisory (SYSTEM.md instruction only — making them native needs deferred IR-enrichment). mechanism strings carry the MIXED-fidelity honesty, including the enforce-lease wired-but-unscoped note when role write_scope is empty.

BackendLifecycle.description: Phase 5 (parity): the grown Backend contract giving Goose and Pi feature-completeness, not just Claude. Each backend OWNS its own artifact lifecycle (the Phase-1 emit seam, extended). Same boundary: imports only ir.graph (+ its helpers) + stdlib; reads its own target lock + artifacts under project_path; never reads manifests/anchor-map/profiles/schema directly (the from-lock recompose path arrives as an IR).

methods.emit: emit(ir: System2Graph, project_path: str) -> list[str] (Phase 1, unchanged)
methods.uninstall: uninstall(project_path: str, overlay_name: str, *, dry_run=False) -> UninstallResult. claude-code: ports composer._uninstall + _uninstall_last_overlay byte-faithfully (recompose-remaining via ir.compose->emit, or revert-to-base on the last overlay; atomic restore). goose/pi: recompose remaining sources (from the additive overlay_sources[] lock key) or remove the full generated tree on the last overlay, atomic restore.
methods.doctor: doctor(project_path: str) -> DoctorReport. claude-code: ports composer.drift_check + _print_doctor_report (status/findings/exit-code byte-faithful). goose: validates each recipe via real `goose recipe validate` (LOUD validator_unavailable when goose absent). pi: validates the extension via discoverAndLoadExtensions / `pi -e` + the synthetic tool_call proven-blocking probe (LOUD validator_unavailable when node/pi absent). Never a silent 'current' when the validator could not run.
methods.recompose_from_lock: recompose_from_lock(ir, project_path, *, dry_run=False) -> list[str]. The CLI reads the target's lock overlay sources via read_lock_overlay_sources, recomposes via ir.compose, and calls emit. Claude reads spec/overlay-manifest.lock; goose/pi read overlay_sources[] from their standalone lock.
methods.lock_path: lock_path(project_path) -> str (the target's lock artifact: spec/overlay-manifest.lock | system2.goose.lock.json | system2.pi.lock.json)
methods.read_lock_overlay_sources: read_lock_overlay_sources(project_path) -> list[str] (the overlay source paths recorded in the target's lock; the parsing lives in the backend that owns the lock format)

constraints: no Claude artifact bytes change (REQ-014 holds); the only intentional non-Claude byte change is the additive overlay_sources[] key on the goose/pi locks (appended last; re-baselines those two goldens once)
the claude-code lifecycle is invocable with the EXACT composer.py flag CLI + exit codes + stdout/stderr (CLI-contract goldens vs the frozen oracle)
goose/pi doctor: LOUD validator_unavailable when the real validator is absent; never a silent 'current' (no-silent-downgrade ethic)

VendoredBundle.description: Phase 5 (C3/G7/NFR-005): the vendored, stdlib-only bundle the plugin ships. RESOLVED: a vendored module SUBTREE (plugin/scripts/_system2_compiler/), NOT a single-file amalgamation — a pure verbatim copy of the compiler's ir/ + backends/ (+ plugin_adapter) so the boundary + stdlib-only properties are exactly the compiler's and byte-identical Claude output is guaranteed by construction. Generated by tools/build_bundle.py. Preserves the plugin's ZERO-DEPENDENCY property (no pip, no submodule, no network).

fields.BUNDLE.json: { compiler_source_sha256: str (hash over sorted (relpath, bytes) of the copied source — the drift anchor), compiler_version: str, generated_from: str (System2-Compiler@<git-rev>), bundled_at: str (EXCLUDED from the hash) }

constraints: stdlib-only (verified by check_no_external_deps over the vendored subtree); plugin runtime deps stay empty (G7)
a pure copy of compiler product source -> byte-identical Claude output by construction (goldens then prove it)
freshness is machine-enforced: tools/check_bundle_fresh.py (CI) + system2:doctor bundle_freshness/bundle_tampered findings (G8/NFR-006)

PluginFlip.description: Phase 5 [PLUGIN]: the convergence flip. RESOLVED: THIN SHIM (not full-replace). composer.py and profiles.py become ~10-line shims delegating to the vendored bundle (via plugin_adapter), preserving the EXACT flag CLI the skills invoke (--doctor/--uninstall/--from-lock/--profile/--save-profile/--profile-op/--profile-*/--base/--overlays/--project/--dry-run/--format/--allow-injection/--allow-newer-schema/--force) + exit codes + stdout/stderr byte-for-byte. --target is hard-pinned to claude-code inside the adapter (the plugin is Claude-only). The pre-flip composer.py is preserved as composer.py.preflip (immutable oracle baseline + one-commit backout target).
constraints: ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/composer.py invocation path + flag surface UNCHANGED -> skills (compose/doctor/profile/init/uninstall) need ZERO changes
plugin_adapter.py is the ONE place the composer.py CLI contract is encoded; pinned by the CLI-contract goldens against the frozen oracle
reversible: restore composer.py/profiles.py from *.preflip + delete _system2_compiler/ = one-commit backout, zero residue
GATE before merge: bundle-equivalence (bundle output == compiler == frozen oracle) empty-diff + CLI-contract goldens empty-diff + the plugin's own System2/evals/ suite green

DriftGuard.description: Phase 5 (C3/G8/NFR-006): machine-enforced vendored-bundle freshness. Two surfaces keyed off BUNDLE.json.compiler_source_sha256.

surfaces.ci_hash_guard: tools/check_bundle_fresh.py: regenerate the bundle from current compiler source, hash, compare to the committed _system2_compiler/ + BUNDLE.json; FAIL CI when stale ('regenerate via build_bundle.py'). A stale bundle cannot merge.
surfaces.doctor_staleness: system2:doctor gains bundle_freshness (recorded provenance: compiler_version/generated_from) + bundle_tampered (the recomputed vendored-subtree hash != BUNDLE.json.compiler_source_sha256 -> a hand-edited bundle). Report-only in the end-user doctor (does not block compose). The authoritative cross-repo (bundle == regenerated-from-source) check is the CI guard.

constraints: deterministic (pure-copy bundler; bundled_at excluded from the hash)
drift-guard self-test: mutate a vendored byte -> CI guard fails AND doctor reports bundle_tampered (teeth)

constraints: status enum is exactly {native, adapted, advisory, unsupported} (REQ-036)
every IR capability must be present (completeness, REQ-031)
for claude-code, all enforced safety capabilities have status 'native' (REQ-034)

GooseRecipe.description: Phase 3: a Goose recipe YAML (orchestrator system2.recipe.yaml or a role agents/<role>.recipe.yaml). Validated by 'goose recipe validate' (the validity oracle). Parent may be YAML/JSON; sub-recipes are YAML-only and CANNOT nest sub_recipes (maps onto 'subagents cannot spawn subagents').

fields.title: str (required)
fields.instructions: str (orchestrator/role persona + gate checklist + delegation contract + advisory capability blocks, rendered from structured IR fields)
fields.parameters: list[object] { key, input_type, requirement, description } -- EVERY declared parameter MUST be referenced via {{ key }} or validation fails ('Unnecessary parameter definitions'); emitter asserts referenced superset-of declared
fields.extensions: list[object] { type: builtin|stdio, name, timeout, bundled } -- e.g. the developer builtin; extensions ADD tools, they cannot GATE builtins
fields.sub_recipes: list[object] { name, path (YAML file), values?: map } -- ONLY on the orchestrator; role sub-recipes MUST NOT declare sub_recipes (no nesting)
fields.settings: object (per-recipe model override from Role.model_hint when present; omitted otherwise) -- exact shape is OQ-G1, resolve via goose recipe validate

constraints: valid per 'goose recipe validate' on goose v1.38.0 (the oracle, AC-G1)
parameters referenced is a superset of parameters declared (else validation fails)
sub-recipes are YAML-only and declare no nested sub_recipes
rendered from structured IR fields (gate_graph/delegation_contract/post_execution/maintenance_loop), NOT from base_template/overlay_inputs (Claude-targeted, not consumed)

GoosePermissionPolicy.description: Phase 3: generated Goose permission policy fragment (project-local goose/permission.yaml) delivering the ADAPTED enforcement for block-dangerous/protect-sensitive. emit writes it under project_path only (pure, home-dir-free); the launcher merges it into the GLOBAL ~/.config/goose/permission.yaml (loud, reversible, opt-in).

fields.user: object keyed by tool name (shell/Bash, Read, Write, Edit) -> { permission: always_allow|ask_before|never_allow }

constraints: dangerous-command set -> never_allow on the shell tool; Read/Write/Edit -> ask_before
paired with GOOSE_MODE=smart_approve (LLM PermissionJudge) set by the launcher
is a permission gate (adapted), NOT a deterministic block (not native); entries emitted in fixed sorted order for a stable global-merge diff
global delivery is the launcher's job; emit never touches $HOME

GooseDegradationReport.description: Phase 3: standalone system2.goose.lock.json (the Goose analogue of the Claude lock's degradation_report; standalone so the claude-code lock format is untouched). Sole machine-readable surface for enforced-vs-advisory on Goose. MUST match goose.json status per capability (AC-G3). Pure function of the IR (no timestamps).

fields.DEGRADATION: str (LOUD headline banner: enforced primitives downgraded to adapted/advisory)
fields.capabilities: object keyed by capability name -> { status: enum(adapted|advisory), mechanism: str, enforced: bool, gated: bool }

constraints: every IR capability appears (completeness; no silent drop; NFR-003 / REQ-033 analogue)
no capability has status 'native' for goose (AC-G3)
report status == backends/capabilities/goose.json status per capability (AC-G3)
adapted caps: enforced=false, gated=true; advisory caps: enforced=false, gated=false (adapted != enforced, T6)

GooseLauncher.description: Phase 3: thin generated run-system2.sh (C6/NFR-007: launcher, never an abstraction). Validate-then-run only; owns the global permission delivery and GOOSE_MODE.
steps: goose recipe validate system2.recipe.yaml && validate each agents/*.recipe.yaml (fail fast)
opt-in merge of goose/permission.yaml into ~/.config/goose/permission.yaml (backup prior file; stricter-wins on conflict; LOUD warning if skipped -> adapted enforcement NOT active)
constraints: no workflow logic / no translation / no policy in bash
generated deterministically
skipping the permission merge prints a LOUD warning (no silent downgrade, NFR-003)

DegradationHelper.description: Phase 4 (PG6): the shared descriptor-driven degradation contract (backends/_degradation.py). Separates policy (which caps, order, native-allowed?) from mechanism (record assembly). BYTE-PRESERVING for claude-code/goose; the enabler for Pi's mixed status.

functions.build_capability_records: build_capability_records(descriptor: dict, ir_capability_union: set[str], *, fields: tuple[str, ...], allow_native: bool = True) -> dict[str, dict]

rules.iteration_order: descriptor 'capabilities' order, filtered to IR-present (matches both existing builders exactly)
rules.record_key_order: exactly the supplied 'fields' tuple order (insertion-ordered; the byte-fidelity crux)
rules.status_to_flags: native => {enforced:true, gated:false}; adapted => {enforced:false, gated:true}; advisory => {both false}; unsupported => {both false}
rules.no_silent_drop: raises ValueError if an IR-present capability is absent from the descriptor (the exact error both builders raise today)
rules.native_guard: raises when allow_native is False and any selected status is 'native' (goose)

byte_preservation: claude-code wrapper: fields=('status','mechanism'), allow_native=True, envelope {backend, capabilities} -> byte-identical to the pre-refactor lock degradation_report

goose wrapper: fields=('status','mechanism','enforced','gated'), allow_native=False, envelope {backend, goose_version_assumed, mode, permission_delivery, DEGRADATION, capabilities} -> byte-identical to the pre-refactor system2.goose.lock.json
pi wrapper: fields=('status','mechanism','enforced','gated'), allow_native=True -> the new MIXED report (native+adapted+advisory in one backend)

PiExtension.description: Phase 4: the generated Pi TypeScript extension (.pi/extensions/system2.ts). A default-export-function module auto-discovered from .pi/extensions/*.ts. Emitted as TEXT by the compiler (never run/transpiled by the compiler; node/pi only in tests). Pi has NO built-in permission system — the generated extension IS the gate. Validity oracle: load via node/pi (discoverAndLoadExtensions / createExtensionRuntime / `pi -e`) + a synthetic-tool_call PROVEN-BLOCKING unit test.
PiExtension.shape: import type { ExtensionAPI, ToolCallEvent, ... } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent"; export default function (pi: ExtensionAPI) { ... }

handlers.on('tool_call'): NATIVE safety gates — fires BEFORE a tool and CAN BLOCK; returns ToolCallEventResult {block?: boolean; reason?: string}. block-dangerous: bash command in the backend-owned dangerous set -> {block:true}. protect-sensitive: read/write/edit/bash touching a backend-owned sensitive path -> {block:true}. enforce-lease: write/edit path outside role write_scope -> {block:true} (wired-but-unscoped + honestly reported when write_scope empty). Uses isToolCallEventType('bash'|'read'|'edit'|'write'|...) narrowing.
handlers.on('agent_end'): ADAPTED budget reporting (a report via ctx.ui.notify / appended summary, NOT a block).
handlers.before_agent_start | context: inject the System2 orchestrator context ({systemPrompt} or {messages}); seam picked empirically (OQ-P2).
handlers.registerCommand('/delegate'): bounded dispatcher: validate role in the 13 (delegation_contract.preferred_order), load the role prompt, dispatch; isolation fidelity native vs adapted per the empirical probe (OQ-P1).

constraints: type-checks against ExtensionAPI and loads under Pi v0.79.9 (AC-P2)
PROVEN-BLOCKING: synthetic tool_call events assert {block:true} for dangerous bash / sensitive read / off-lease write, and not-blocked for benign inputs (AC-P3)
dangerous-command + sensitive-path pattern sets are BACKEND-OWNED defaults (keeps the IR neutral; mirrors goose._DANGEROUS_COMMANDS)
every IR-derived string interpolated into the .ts is escaped for a TS literal (no raw splice; REQ-042 injection posture preserved)
deterministic: sorted pattern sets, stable escaping, LF endings, single trailing newline; emit(ir) twice byte-identical

PiArtifactSet.description: Phase 4: the full set of files PiBackend.emit writes under project_path. Deterministic, sorted, pure function of the IR (no timestamps). emit writes only under project_path; never touches $HOME / the user's real ~/.pi.

files..pi/extensions/system2.ts: the generated TS gate + /delegate dispatcher + commands + context injection (see PiExtension)
files..pi/SYSTEM.md: orchestrator context from the structured IR (gate graph 0->5, delegation contract, post-exec/maintenance policy, overlay-contributed material, advisory NOT-ENFORCED blocks, native/adapted notes)
files.AGENTS.md: short auto-loaded project context: System2 one-liner, 13-role inventory, gate pipeline, pointers to SYSTEM.md/skills/the /delegate command
files..pi/prompts/orchestrator.md: orchestrator prompt template (drive the gate graph, delegate via /delegate)
files..pi/prompts/role-<name>.md: one prompt template per role of the 13: persona + gate-role + write-scope + model-hint note + native/adapted/advisory capability notes
files..pi/skills/system2-init/SKILL.md: skill: set up / start the System2 workflow
files..pi/skills/system2-compose/SKILL.md: skill: run the gate pipeline; use /delegate for the 13 roles; the delegation contract
files..pi/skills/system2-doctor/SKILL.md: skill: verify the extension loads and the gates are live (operator analogue of the proven-blocking test)

constraints: 13 roles -> 13 role prompt templates + /delegate targets (AC-P6)
renders from the STRUCTURED IR fields only; does NOT consume base_template / overlay_inputs (AC-P7)
emitted as TEXT (TS + markdown + JSON); stdlib-only compiler; no node/TS dependency in the compiler

PiDegradationReport.description: Phase 4: standalone system2.pi.lock.json — the FIRST mixed-status degradation report (native + adapted + advisory in one backend). Built via the shared backends/_degradation helper (allow_native=True, fields=('status','mechanism','enforced','gated')). Standalone so the claude-code lock is untouched (same posture as the goose lock). Pure function of the IR (no timestamps). MUST match pi.json status per capability.

fields.subagent_isolation: str ('native'|'adapted', per the empirical /delegate isolation probe — OQ-P1)
fields.FIDELITY: str (headline banner: which gates are NATIVE blocks vs ADAPTED report vs ADVISORY instruction; includes the enforce-lease wired-but-unscoped note when write_scope is empty)
fields.capabilities: object keyed by capability name -> { status: enum(native|adapted|advisory), mechanism: str, enforced: bool, gated: bool }

constraints: every IR capability appears (completeness; no silent drop; NFR-003/REQ-033 analogue)
MIXES statuses: enforce-lease/block-dangerous/protect-sensitive = native; budget = adapted; format/typecheck = advisory (AC-P4)
report status == backends/capabilities/pi.json status per capability (AC-P4)
flags follow the status->flags rule (native=>enforced:true,gated:false; adapted=>enforced:false,gated:true; advisory=>both false)

enforce-lease honesty: when role write_scope is empty, status stays native (the mechanism — a hard pre-execution block — is real) but the mechanism text + FIDELITY banner state it is wired-but-UNSCOPED until IR-enrichment (OQ-P3); never a silent vacuous native claim (T8)

CLIArgs.description: system2 (additive, opt-in; REQ-049). Phase 1: a single implicit 'compile'. Phase 3/4 extend --target to goose/pi. Phase 5 (parity): a subcommand dispatcher reaching FULL parity with composer.py — compile | uninstall | doctor | from-lock | profile {list|inspect|save|create|edit|delete} — plus --allow-injection/--force. `system2 compile` (no subcommand) stays back-compatible. Profiles are harness-NEUTRAL (no --target).

subcommands.doctor: --target {…} --base B --project P [--format …]  (exit 0 if current else 1; goose/pi LOUD validator_unavailable when absent)
subcommands.from-lock: --target {…} --base B --project P [--dry-run] [--allow-injection] [--allow-newer-schema] [--format …]  (sugar for compile --from-lock; own verb for skill-contract parity)
subcommands.profile: {list | inspect NAME | save NAME | create NAME --paths P | edit NAME [--add P]… [--remove OVERLAY]… | delete NAME} [--project P] [--force] [--format …]  (harness-neutral; writes only ~/.system2/profiles.json; rejects --dry-run on mutations; emits the pre-mutation active_in_project signal)

args.--target: required for compile/uninstall/doctor/from-lock; enum {claude-code, goose, pi}; NOT used by profile (harness-neutral)
args.--profile: NAME; xor with --overlays/--from-lock; routes through profile resolution; hard-fail on unknown/stale (ported _activate_profile)
args.--overlays: comma-separated overlay source paths; xor with --profile/--from-lock
args.--from-lock: recompose from the target's lock overlay sources (claude: spec/overlay-manifest.lock; goose/pi: overlay_sources[])
args.--name: overlay name to uninstall (kebab-case; ported _uninstall validation)
args.--paths / --add / --remove: profile create paths / edit add+remove (repeatable), ported from --profile-paths/--profile-add/--profile-remove
args.--project: required; target project root (must not be inside --base, REQ-020)
args.--dry-run: compute graph + files_to_write, write nothing (REQ-023); REJECTED on profile mutations (exact ported error)
args.--allow-injection: proceed despite prompt-injection warnings in write mode (compile/uninstall/from-lock); else refuse with exit 4 + exact message (ported injection gate)
args.--force: overwrite an existing profile on save/create

constraints: the claude-code path of every verb reproduces the frozen oracle's args/exit-codes/stdout/stderr byte-for-byte (CLI-contract goldens)
mutual-exclusion + sub-flag rejection rules ported verbatim (profile xor overlays xor from-lock xor uninstall; --dry-run rejected on mutations)

OracleLock.description: evals/oracle.lock.json (REQ-006/007). Discoverable hash-pin of the frozen oracle and its dependencies.

ComparisonPolicy.description: Per-artifact-class golden comparison policy (REQ-004/005). Default byte-identical; all classes byte-identical this cycle (OPEN-1).
